summary: Migration inventory for every documentation link the Atlas GIS registry exposes. Classifies audience, canonical owner and public destination before any UI link is changed, so evidence is not hidden and developer documentation is not promoted as public narrative. Public routes are proposals: the Handbook route model is fixed by KAN-410.

documents.title: VMN data dictionary
documents.notes: Field meanings, controlled vocabularies and temporal conventions are reader-facing; the FGB build contracts and the spec section numbers are not. Pattern B: an authored data-fields record cites the canonical field IDs, and the full dictionary stays reachable under Advanced/Technical.
documents.outcomeNote: The reader-facing half - status vocabulary, route types, phases, locator rules - is now an authored data-fields record. The machine schema stays in the repository as an Advanced link, which is what Pattern B is for.

documents.title: VMN source log
documents.notes: The historical authorities behind every VMN feature, plus the publication rules. Wholly reader-facing and short enough to render as-is (Pattern A). Feature-level citations already resolve through it, so it must not stay behind a GitHub hop.
documents.outcomeNote: Projected whole, as the audit proposed. It was already wholly reader-facing. The bibliography page, which used to send readers to GitHub for it, now links this route.

documents.title: VMN essay-Atlas deep-link guide
documents.notes: A specification of Atlas URL parameters and an anchor validation table. The reader-facing equivalent of this document is the Atlas affordance itself - "Copy this view" (KAN-405) - not a page of parameter tables. Demote from first-level to Advanced/Technical; do not publish.
documents.outcomeNote: Demoted rather than published, as the audit proposed. It is no longer a first-level peer of the source log because catalogue rows carry no documentation clusters at all; it survives as an Advanced link on the three VMN layer records. Its reader-facing equivalent is the Atlas share contract itself.

documents.title: HSE data dictionary
documents.notes: Same split as the VMN dictionary. The participation classes, evidence types and certainty vocabulary are exactly what a reader needs to interpret the map; the compile outputs, promotion rules and release manifest are not.
documents.outcomeNote: Participation classes, evidence types and certainty are published in reader language; compile outputs and promotion rules stay technical.

documents.title: HSE decisions log
documents.notes: Carries genuinely reader-facing editorial reasoning ("Two different fours", "Bruges in the past tense", the vocabulary decisions) interleaved with stable-ID and build-contract governance. Pattern B: publish the curated editorial decisions; the full log stays technical. This document also holds the network-not-territory rationale that KAN-418 requires be publicly legible.
documents.outcomeNote: Split as KAN-414 required. The historiographical decision - the League held privileges in places, not ground between them - is published. Stable IDs, build contracts and the superseded vertical-slice boundary stay in the repository, because they are not historical arguments.

documents.title: CCD data dictionary
documents.notes: 416 lines, mostly CSV schemas and governance tables. The reader-facing minority - the promotion ladder, the confidence and attestation-class vocabularies, and the two-tier release contract - is what the Atlas facets expose, so it must surface publicly while the schemas stay technical.
documents.outcomeNote: The reader-facing minority of a 416-line document: confidence, geometry provenance, line types, attestation classes, review state, sovereignty. The CSV schemas stay technical.

documents.title: Corpus Chartarum Daciae programme README
documents.notes: The only current link whose public owner already exists: the programme index shipped in KAN-370. The layer should point at that route, not at the README. The README keeps the identifier, immutability and gate-running material as technical documentation.
documents.outcomeNote: The only entry whose public owner already existed. The layer record now links the KAN-370 programme index; the README keeps the identifier, immutability and gate-running material as technical documentation.

documents.title: The shared Dacia GIS family
documents.notes: The heaviest reuse in the registry: five layers cite this one document, and four of them are asking it for their own per-layer explanation. Migration must split it into one shared method record (the rule the family is built on, the geometry_provenance contract) plus per-layer records that reference it. Copying the shared prose into five layer pages would create exactly the duplicate scholarly identity KAN-418 forbids.
documents.outcomeNote: DEVIATION from the audit, which proposed Pattern B. Projected whole instead: the document is wholly public-scholarly, and one projected method referenced by five layer records is a stronger guarantee against duplication than five authored records that each retell it. The hazard the audit named is closed by referencesDocIds rather than by splitting the prose.

documents.title: Treaty and frontier source ledger, 1829-1947
documents.notes: Frozen instruments, interpretation and confidence, the editorial geometry rule and the rights posture, in reader-facing prose and bound to one layer. This is the gold-standard target for KAN-413: the pattern every other layer is measured against.
documents.outcomeNote: Projected whole, as the audit proposed. It is the gold-standard evidence record the treaty-frontier layer page cites for instrument-by-instrument detail.

layerCoverage.note: Assessed against what a published historical or evidential layer owes a reader: an explanation of the claim and a record of the evidence behind it. Context layers take a minimal-context exemption. "partial" means some public function is documented and at least one required one is not. Layers registered after the cutover are recorded as covered on arrival: the release gate refuses a published or in-review layer without a public record, so there is no state in which one of them could be outstanding.

layers.note: Neutral base geography. Minimal-context exemption: source, licence and attribution on the layer record are sufficient.

Neutral base geography. Minimal-context exemption.

Minimal-context exemption, but conditional: the present-day boundary layer must carry a visible anachronism warning wherever it is drawn over historical material (KAN-402 inspector, KAN-418 step 8). The exemption covers documentation depth, not the warning.

No documentation link of any kind, and it is an evidence layer. A reader cannot currently learn how a depicted extent was derived, what precision it claims, or that it describes the map rather than the ground. Must be closed before first public GIS release.

The layer carries an AWMC/Barrington attribution and an ODbL licence in its record, but nothing explains what "imperial extent" means as a claim, how the frontier was drawn, or how it relates to the Dacia material it frames. The most visible unsourced historical layer in the registry.

Same as venetian-ports. Missing the reader-facing statement about clipping to the coastline and what a phased fill does and does not claim about control.

The "may not be cited as established evidence" condition exists only in the layer description. It needs a public record stating the review gate, the two-tier contract and the citation restriction.

As dacia-roman-sites. The Hertslet basis for the phases is in the attribution string, not in a citable record.

nonRegistryLinks.notes: A first-level GitHub link in reader-facing prose on a public page: feature-level citations are told to resolve through it. Repoint to the VMN sources route when it exists.
nonRegistryLinks.outcomeNote: Repointed at cutover (KAN-418). The bibliography no longer sends a reader to GitHub to resolve a feature-level citation.

nonRegistryLinks.notes: As above: repoint to the VMN data-fields route, keeping the raw dictionary under Advanced/Technical.

The only Confluence URL anywhere in the data or the site. It is a source row cited by one provisional HSE evidence claim (hse-claim-lubeck-leading), and it does not reach the built output today. Not a live public defect - but it becomes one the moment HSE sources are published, which KAN-414 is going to do. The claim it supports is already marked superseded, so the fix is to retire the citation rather than to publish the URL. Guarded by a test.
nonRegistryLinks.outcomeNote: Still the only Confluence URL in the data, still absent from the built output, and now guarded twice: by the inventory test and by validate-handbook.mjs, which fails the build on any governance URL anywhere in dist/. KAN-414 published the HSE sources without promoting it; retiring the superseded claim that cites it remains open.

nonRegistryLinks.notes: A link to the released CND 0.1 data tree, surfaced by the public programme index. Legitimately technical: it is the download/reuse gateway, and KAN-416 gives it a proper citation and data-reuse surface. Keep, but present it as Advanced/Technical rather than as documentation.
nonRegistryLinks.outcomeNote: Kept as the data-reuse gateway on the programme index, which is its correct role.

retirements.rationale: Not obsolete, but wrongly promoted: three layers carry it as a first-level peer of their source log. Its reader-facing function is served by the Atlas "Copy this view" affordance (KAN-405). Demote to Advanced/Technical on all three VMN layers.

Superseded as a public destination by /programmes/corpus-chartarum-daciae/ (KAN-370). The "Programme" link on dacia-attestations should resolve to the site route; the README stays as technical documentation.

duplicationRisks.risk: Five layers cite one document, four of them for their own layer explanation. Naive migration would copy the shared prose into five layer pages and create five competing owners of one method. Split into a single method record plus per-layer records that reference it.
One dictionary, three layers. The public data-fields record must be programme-scoped, not per-layer.
Programme-scoped decisions; must not be restated per layer.
Programme-scoped source log, additionally cited from the public bibliography. One owner, three referents.

Repeated across all three VMN layers as a first-level peer link. The duplication is not the main problem here - the promotion is - but it is why the demotion has to happen in one place rather than three.

Cited by both CND attestation tiers. The public data-fields record must be programme-scoped and must state the two-tier contract once, so the reviewed and research layers cannot end up explaining the review gate differently.

cutover.summary: Every inventoried entry has an outcome. Seven documents are replaced by or split into public routes, one is repointed to a public owner that already existed, and one is retained as technical-only with its reason recorded. No entry is unaccounted for, and no first-level GitHub or Confluence documentation link remains in a reader-facing page.
cutover.crusadesDependency: KAN-388 has registered no Atlas layers, so no Crusades layer exists to inherit the public documentation contract. This is recorded as a mandatory publication dependency for the first public GIS release rather than as a completed check: whichever ticket registers the first Crusades layer must give it a public record, and the KAN-412 coverage report plus validate-handbook.mjs will fail the build until it does.
